target: Buenas tardes, ¿cómo te llamas?
english: Good afternoon, what is your name?
tip: 'Tú' is informal – use 'te' forms with friends, family, and people your age.

target: Vivo en el segundo piso.
english: I live on the second floor.
tip: Segundo keeps its full shape before a noun: el segundo piso. Only primero and tercero drop the -o there (primer piso, tercer piso) – the other ordinals never shorten.

target: Necesito un bolígrafo para firmar.
english: I need a pen to sign.
tip: Para before an infinitive means 'in order to': para firmar = so I can sign. English hides purpose in a bare 'to'; Spanish must flag it with para.

target: Mi padre tiene cincuenta años.
english: My father is fifty years old.
tip: Spanish uses 'tener' (to have) for age: 'tiene X años' = is X years old. English uses 'to be' but Spanish literally 'has' years.

target: Buenas noches, espero que hayas tenido un buen día.
english: Good evening, I hope you've had a good day.
tip: Espero que flips the verb into subjunctive: hayas tenido, not has tenido. A hope isn't a fact, and Spanish stamps that uncertainty right onto the verb.

target: Estoy buscando un nuevo trabajo.
english: I'm looking for a new job.
tip: 'Nuevo trabajo' (nuevo first) = new-to-me, another one. Trabajo nuevo = brand-new. Position slides nuevo between 'different' and 'freshly made'.

target: Quiero mucho a mis hijos.
english: I love my children very much.
tip: 'Quiero' here means 'I love' – querer covers both wanting and loving; context decides.

target: Nos despedimos en el aeropuerto.
english: We said goodbye at the airport.
tip: 'Despedirse' is reflexive: nos despedimos = we said goodbye. The reflexive marks the action affects the subject.

target: El sábado vamos al mercado.
english: On Saturday we go to the market.
tip: No word for 'on': 'el sábado' alone means ON Saturday. The article does the work – and los sábados means every Saturday.

target: Las noticias de hoy son buenas.
english: Today's news is good.
tip: 'Noticias' is plural – Spanish counts news piece by piece. So today's news 'son buenas': plural noun, plural verb, plural adjective.

target: Ellos viven cerca de la playa.
english: They live near the beach.
tip: Near needs de: 'cerca de la playa'. English skips the 'of' (near the beach); Spanish never does – cerca de, lejos de, always.

target: El restaurante abre a las siete.
english: The restaurant opens at seven.
tip: Why las in 'a las siete'? Spanish counts the hours: at the seven (hours). Times take the article – a la una, a las dos, a las siete.

target: Después del almuerzo tomo un café.
english: After lunch I have a coffee.
tip: 'Tomo' here means 'I drink' – tomar means both 'to take' and 'to drink'. Context makes it clear.

target: Leo un libro antes de dormir.
english: I read a book before sleeping.
tip: 'Before sleeping'? Spanish bans -ing after prepositions. After antes de comes the infinitive: 'antes de dormir', never a gerund.

target: Ella cree que es buena idea.
english: She thinks it's a good idea.
tip: English drops 'that': she thinks it's a good idea. Spanish never drops que – 'cree que es buena idea'. Skipping que sounds broken.

target: En noviembre ya empieza el frío.
english: In November the cold weather starts.
tip: Subject after the verb: 'empieza el frío' – literally 'starts the cold'. Spanish happily flips the order when the subject is the news.

target: El agua está muy fría hoy.
english: The water is very cold today.
tip: "El agua" – feminine noun using "el" for sound: feminine nouns starting with stressed "a-" take "el" not "la" but stay feminine: "el agua fría."

target: Mi hermano mayor tiene treinta años.
english: My older brother is thirty years old.
tip: 'Hermano mayor' isn't the bigger brother – mayor means older. Age uses mayor/menor, size uses grande/pequeño.

target: Yo duermo muy poco entre semana.
english: I sleep very little during the week.
tip: Duermo, not dormo: the o swells to ue exactly where stress hits the stem. In dormimos the stress moves to -i-, so the o survives untouched.

target: Duermo muy mal cuando hace calor.
english: I sleep very badly when it's hot.
tip: How you do it = mal (adverb); what it is = malo (adjective). 'Duermo muy mal' – sleeping badly, so mal. Malo would describe the sleep itself.

target: Cierro la ventana porque hace frío.
english: I close the window because it's cold.
tip: One word 'porque' = because; split with accent ¿por qué? = why. The question uses por qué, the answer uses porque: 'porque hace frío'.

target: Quiero un billete de ida y vuelta.
english: I want a round-trip ticket.
tip: "ida y vuelta" – literally "go and return."

target: Adiós, nos vemos mañana por la mañana!
english: Goodbye, see you tomorrow morning!
tip: 'Mañana' means both tomorrow and morning. Need both? 'Mañana por la mañana' = tomorrow morning – the article la marks the time-of-day one.

target: Ella es muy alta para su edad.
english: She's very tall for her age.
tip: Ser + physical traits: "Es alto." Ser for characteristics seen as defining, not temporary.

target: Por poco perdemos el avión de vuelta.
english: We almost missed the return flight.
tip: "Por poco" + present tense = almost (did something). A near-miss construction.

target: La reunión es en la sala tres.
english: The meeting is in room three.
tip: Location takes estar – except events! Meetings happen, so ser: 'la reunión es en la sala tres'. Where things sit = estar; where they take place = ser.

target: Mi asiento está cerca de la ventana.
english: My seat is near the window.
tip: "Estar" for location. The seat IS (located) near the window.

target: Lo necesito para mañana a primera hora.
english: I need it first thing tomorrow morning.
tip: 'A primera hora' – at first hour – is Spanish for 'first thing in the morning'. Para mañana a primera hora = by early tomorrow.

target: El sofá del salón es muy cómodo.
english: The living room couch is very comfortable.
tip: 'Salón' isn't a salon – it's the living room. 'El sofá del salón' = the living-room couch. A hair salon is a peluquería.

target: El tren al trabajo tarda treinta minutos.
english: The train to work takes thirty minutes.
tip: One verb means 'to take (time)': tardar. 'El tren tarda treinta minutos' – no extra words needed. Cousin of tarde: late.
